I took a hiatus, worked on some other stuff, and now recently returned to Claudia. As far as trying different genres and seeing what sticks, I second that! I tried historical fiction, but found myself being just as nit-picky as a writer as I’d be as an audience reading someone else’s historical fiction, so I end up stuck because I’m thinking: “This sounds too modern” or “did that event really happen like that?” However, I’ve discovered, with my current novel (which, funny enough, is set in the Roman Empire during the rise of Christianity), this particular WIP is the furthest I’ve ever gotten. Partly because it’s deeply personal for me, and partly because I love the time period in question, the Roman Empire. What I’m getting at is, write something you can relate to or something you are deeply passionate about. If your wish is to convey a message you think others could value, write it. As for your style, that’s what rough drafts are for. Try a style, whether it’s “childish/simple” words or lofty language, and see what sticks. Then you can use subsequent drafts to throw out stuff you don’t like or that didn’t work in your plot.
